image_description: A close-up, slightly low-angle shot of a dual-headed traffic light assembly mounted on a metal pole. The left signal head displays an illuminated amber light at the top, with two unlit blue-tinted lenses below it. The right signal head displays an illuminated red light at the top, an unlit red lens in the middle, and an unlit blue-tinted lens at the bottom. The background shows a street scene with parked cars (a blue van and a silver sedan) and a building facade, rendered with a painterly, textured aesthetic.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The entire image exhibits a strong 'painterly' or oil-painting filter effect, causing loss of fine detail, smearing of edges, and unnatural noise patterns, particularly on the cars and building in the background.
The housing lacks rigid geometric integrity. The boundaries between the individual light hoods and the main body are soft and fused, appearing like melted wax rather than assembled metal parts.

Semantic error: The unlit lenses are rendered as bright blue opaque circles. Real traffic light lenses are dark (black/dark red/green) when unlit. This indicates a failure to understand the physical properties of the object.
The blue van on the left has warped geometry; the wheel wells and door lines are wavy and inconsistent with rigid automotive design.
